headline: Before the file. A child in care.
intro: Training that helps probation, prison, police, housing and health staff see the care experience behind the file.

problem.question: His 40-page file never mentions his eight years in care.
without: A sharp reply read as hostility
No call to the leaving care team
with: Staff ask about care, with consent
Missed appointments read for the reason
problem.standards: Prisons are now asked to identify care experience and, with consent, contact the council. Since 30 September 2026 care leavers under 25 can't be found intentionally homeless.
problem.evidence: Most of the changes cost nothing: a text reminder, a clearer letter, a named worker and a first call to the leaving care team.

outcomes: Recognise signs someone grew up in care when it isn't on the file, and ask in a way that respects consent.
Describe a missed appointment or a sharp reply from the side of someone whose adults kept leaving.
Explain care experienced and care leaver, personal advisers up to 25, and the HMPPS and homelessness changes.
Use Bowlby and the window of tolerance to explain how early trauma shapes trust and responses to authority.
Apply the six principles of trauma-informed practice to appointments, letters and first conversations.
Find the leaving care team and local offer, and plan when to involve the personal adviser.

pillars.title: Six principles for the next appointment
pillars.stance: They were a child in care first
pillars.stance_line: The government's working definition of trauma-informed practice sets out six principles. We turn them into front-desk practice.
items: Short waits and a calm opening, so people can take in what they're told.
A named worker who does what they said they would.
Options on times and on how to get in touch.
Plan changes with the person and their personal adviser.
Start from what the person can do, not the warning.
Recognise the person's history and identity, including care.
pillars.base: Office for Health Improvement and Disparities, working definition of trauma-informed practice (2022), with Bowlby's attachment theory and Siegel's window of tolerance.

facilitator.name: Luke Rodgers BEM
facilitator.line: From care leaver to care leader
paras: Luke went into care at 10. He has spent his career inside children's services as a consultant, trainer and keynote speaker, and is CEO of The Care Leaders.

He has worked with councils and the NHS nationally on how services see the person behind the label, including Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent, where he trained more than 400 staff across health, social care and education.
He led the national engagement on England's new fostering standards for the Department for Education, and knows the system a care-experienced adult grew up in.
He was a Knowledge Equity Fellow at Saïd Business School, University of Oxford, and was awarded the British Empire Medal in 2018 for commitment to children and families.
